definitions.explanation: Everyday spoken language as opposed to literary or written language. In Japanese linguistics, contrasts with {文語|ぶんご} (classical/literary language).

examples.japanese: {口語|こうご}{体|たい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}いて→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。

⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{口語|こうご}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{文章|ぶんしょう}→文章：02957_bunshou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{使|つか}わない→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: This expression is used in spoken language but not in writing.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{口語|こうご}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{文語|ぶんご}→文語：12991_bungo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦かなり→かなり：01149_kanari⟧⟦{異|こと}なる→異なる：02101_kotonaru⟧。
examples.english: Japanese grammar differs considerably between spoken and literary language.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japanese linguistics, {口語|こうご} specifically refers to modern spoken/colloquial Japanese, contrasting with ⟦{文語|ぶんご}→文語：12991_bungo⟧ (classical literary Japanese based on Heian-era grammar). This distinction is important in Japanese education, where students learn both {口語|こうご}⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧ (modern grammar) and ⟦{文語|ぶんご}→文語：12991_bungo⟧⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧ (classical grammar).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {口語|こうご}{体|たい}: colloquial style
- {口語|こうご}⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧: colloquial/modern grammar
- {口語|こうご}⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧: colloquial expression
- {口語|こうご}⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧: colloquial, conversational
